explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge with human evaluation on the same 100 instances from MSC dataset, reports Cohen's kappa agreement metrics between LLM and human annotators

prompts.notes: Prompt for LLM judge is presented in Appendix D.3, following methodology from prior work

guidelines.notes: Human annotators followed the same instruction used in the LLM judge prompt, evaluating whether generated response matches ground truth as binary Yes/No

sample_size.notes: 100 randomly sampled instances from MSC dataset used for both LLM and human evaluation

quantitative_scores.notes: Agreement between LLM and Human A
Agreement between LLM and Human B

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Cohen's Kappa interpretation standard (0.61-0.80 considered substantial)

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-a-judge shows substantial agreement with human evaluations (κ=0.69-0.71), comparable to human-human agreement (κ=0.82), demonstrating reliable validation of LLM judgments against human annotations.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluated the same Truth criterion (whether generated response matches ground truth) using identical binary Yes/No scale
